name: Poland
headline: Poland: +3.7% growth in 2025, 3.6% inflation, debt 60% of GDP
sections: Poland is a $1.04 trillion economy (2025), the world's 22nd-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +3.7% in 2025, close to the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $54K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 15.0% of GDP (2025).

Consumer prices rose 3.6% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 14.4% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 3.1% (2025), below the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 10.7% (2025).
Gross government debt is 60% of GDP (2025), a moderate level that has risen from 57% in 2020. The general government balance is −7.3% of GDP (2025), a deficit beyond the common 3% benchmark.
The current account balance is −1.0% of GDP (2025). Trade equals 97% of GDP (2025), a fairly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 2.0% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 82% of GDP by 2031, still rising from today's level. Life expectancy is 78.4 years (2024). Population: 36.5 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
